title: Hallucination as an Upper Bound: A New Perspective on Text-to-Image Evaluation

bias_targets.methodology: Proposes a taxonomy to evaluate unprompted gender assignments (e.g., text-to-image models defaulting to a male figure for the neutral prompt 'a doctor') by classifying them as 'attribute hallucinations'.
Proposes identifying implicit cultural defaults (e.g., models consistently generating a tall, tiered, white Western-style cake for the prompt 'a wedding cake') as a form of 'attribute hallucination'.

Proposes evaluating stereotyped activities and layout defaults (e.g., a prompt for 'a woman and a laptop' consistently showing her typing in a work scenario) by categorizing them as 'relation hallucinations'.
